section_summary.extract_value: This section details the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2), a 10-item instrument used to measure positive body image. It describes the scale's 5-point response format and highlights its good internal reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .91–.94) and 3-week stability (r = .90) as established in samples of college and community women and men, and 14- and 15-year-old girls by other researchers. The text indicates that 'Participants' in the current paper answered this scale, referring to one study.
section_summary.evidence_source: 2.2.2. Body appreciation Participants answered the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015a), a 10-item scale measuring positive body image. All items are answered on a 5-point scale, ranging from 1 (Never) to 5 (Always). The BAS-2 is composed of one dimension with good internal reliability (Cronbach = .91–.94) and 3-week stability, r = .90 in samples of college and community women and men (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015a; Webb, 2015). Halliwell et al. (2015) found good internal reliability (Cronbach = .94–.95) in BAS-2 scores among a group of 14- and 15-year-old girls.
